key_insight: PackForcing shows that training autoregressive video diffusion models on short clips is sufficient for stable long-video sampling and long-context inference by managing history with a three-partition KV-cache.
problem_solved: Addresses intractable linear KV-cache growth, temporal repetition, and compounding errors that prevent scalable, high-quality long-video generation.
method: Three-partition KV-cache that separates historical context into: sink tokens (persistent anchors), compact/packed summaries of older context, and an active recent-context cache to limit growth and repetition.

Training on short video clips with the PackForcing cache strategy so the model learns to rely on compacted history and therefore generalizes to arbitrarily long sampling without linear memory scaling.
Sampling-time mechanics that read from the three partitions to reconstruct long-range context while avoiding repeated content and reducing error propagation.
impact: Enables scalable long-video generation with much lower memory and compute cost, making long-context autoregressive diffusion practical for researchers and developers building video generation and long-horizon sequence models.

Flowchart showing short-clip training -> PackForcing sampling -> long-video output (emphasizing no long-clip training needed)
paper_title: PackForcing: Short Video Training Suffices for Long Video Sampling and Long Context Inference
paper_authors: Xiaofeng Mao, Shaohao Rui, Kaining Ying, Bo Zheng, Chuanhao Li
